subject: Post-call: dedicated capacity pricing + $/1M token targets (Nimbus Health)
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Alice Chen <alice@nimbushealth.com>, procurement@nimbushealth.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: dedicated capacity pricing + $/1M token targets (Nimbus Health)

Hi Alice — thanks for the time today. Quick recap and next steps from our side, plus a couple of clarifying questions so we can get you a firm reserved-capacity quote.

Call recap (high level)
- Primary goal: deploy Redwood Dedicated for real-time clinical assistance and patient messaging (mixed short prompts + 1–2 long-form generation flows).
- Expected monthly usage: ~120M generated tokens (customer estimate).
- Latency SLO: p95 < 250ms for 512-token responses; expected concurrency ~30–50 active users during peaks.
- Throughput target: sustained ~5k tokens/sec, peak bursts to ~20k tokens/sec.
- Target unit economics: looking to land in the ~$150–$250 / 1M tokens range depending on configuration and term.
- GPUs discussed: preference for H100 for throughput, but open to A100 80GB if cost/availability is better.

Questions we need answered to finalize the reserved quote (please reply inline):
1) Can you confirm the 120M tokens/month is the aggregated total across all flows (yes/no)?
2) Any hard budget constraints for monthly spend (range is fine)?
3) Are there regulatory or networking constraints that would push you to Private/VPC instead of hosted Dedicated?

What we’ll deliver next
- Price options for 3 configurations: 4x H100 reserved; 8x A100 80GB reserved; and hybrid (4x A100 + autoscale). Each will include expected sustained throughput, burst capacity, and estimated $/1M tokens.
- A short workbook (attached) with token modeling and unit-econ assumptions so you can tweak prompts.
- A provisional dedicated configuration PDF that shows autoscale and canary rollout options.

Next steps suggested
- Alice to confirm monthly token aggregate and budget band.
- We’ll provide a formal quote and a 12-month vs 3-month pricing comparison (commit tiers affect unit $/1M).

Attaching: nimbus_pricing_workbook_v1.xlsx, provisional_dedicated_config.pdf

Thanks — I’ll hold on the formal quote until I get the two data points above.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

Subject: Re: Post-call: dedicated capacity pricing + $/1M token targets (Nimbus Health)

Hi Karthik — thanks for the recap, that matches our notes. Quick answers inline: 

1) Confirming 120M tokens/month is the aggregate across all flows (patient messages + clinical assistant + batch summaries).
2) Budget: our procurement lead gave us a target range of $18k–$36k / month (we expect to lean toward the middle if unit economics make sense).
3) We require VPC connectivity and business-associate agreements for PHI handling; technically we can do Redwood Dedicated in a VPC setup.

A few more details that will help your calc:
- Token mix: ~70% short messages (avg 60 tokens), 25% medium (avg 350 tokens), 5% long summaries (avg 1,200 tokens).
- Peak concurrency window is 09:00–11:00 PT and 17:00–19:00 PT for East coast usage overlap.

Procurement will review the workbook and I’ll push for a 12-month commit if we see the price reduce to <$220 / 1M tokens.

Procurement contact: Javier Morales <javier.morales@nimbushealth.com>

Thanks — Alice

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Alice Chen <alice@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: dedicated capacity pricing + $/1M token targets (Nimbus Health)

Thanks Alice — that helps a lot. Based on the usage shape and target budget band, here are our recommended options and rough unit-econ math (ballpark; final numbers after procurement confirmation and term selection):

Option A — Performance-first (recommended for latency-sensitive flows)
- Config: 4x NVIDIA H100 (reserved), autoscale policy to +4 H100 for bursts (manual/canary rules).
- Expected sustained throughput: ~5k tokens/sec across the pool; burst up to ~20k tokens/sec when autoscaled.
- Estimated 12-month committed price: ~$180 / 1M tokens (assumes quantization-friendly model + batching/caching).
- Estimated monthly cost: ~$21.6k for 120M tokens (@$180/1M).

Option B — Cost-first (A100-focused)
- Config: 8x NVIDIA A100 80GB (reserved), autoscale to +4 A100 for bursts.
- Sustained throughput similar (~4.5–6k tokens/sec depending on model), slightly higher latency p95 vs H100 on large batches.
- Estimated 12-month committed price: ~$155–$170 / 1M tokens depending on quantization.
- Estimated monthly cost: $18.6k–$20.4k for 120M tokens.

Option C — Hybrid / shorter term
- Config: 3x H100 + 4x A100, shorter 3-month commit, higher unit price (~$220/1M).
- Good for validating product-market fit before full commit.

Assumptions and levers that change $/1M tokens
- Quantization & model selection (int8/4-bit) reduces GPU cycles per token by ~15–30%.
- Prefix/KV caching and batching reduces effective generated tokens by ~8–12% for chat-style flows.
- Longer commit term (12+ months) and minimum monthly token commitment moves price down by one tier.

Attachments: I pushed an updated workbook that includes the above scenarios and an assumptions tab (nimbus_pricing_workbook_v1.xlsx). Also attaching a provisional config diagram (provisional_dedicated_config.pdf).

If these options look reasonable I’ll have Ben (cc’d) run a quick validation of the throughput numbers against your expected token mix and then we can lock a formal quote.

Next steps:
- Ben to validate throughput math and expected p95s for your 60/350/1200 token distribution.
- Ben/Karthik to produce formal quote for 12-month committed Option A & B.
- Alice to route to Procurement (Javier) for PO timetable.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
